steps.caption: All living things carry out three life processes: nutrition, sensitivity and reproduction.

Nutrition is the process through which living things get raw materials and energy from food. They need raw materials to grow and repair their bodies, and energy to carry out activities such as movement and reproduction.
Animals feed on other living things. Herbivores eat plants, carnivores eat other animals and omnivores eat both plants and other animals. The bear is an omnivore: its food is plants, fish and meat.
Plants make their own food. They take in water, mineral salts and carbon dioxide, and they use energy from sunlight. This process is called photosynthesis.
Memory trick: herbi sounds like herbs, so a herbivore eats plants. Omni means all, so an omnivore eats all kinds of food: plants and other animals.

Sensitivity is the process through which living things detect and respond to changes in their environment. Animals detect information through their sense organs and respond with movement, so they can get food or get away from a possible threat.
Plants do not have sense organs and they cannot move about. However, they detect and respond to changes too. For instance, trees lose their leaves in autumn.

steps.caption: Reproduction is the process through which all living things produce offspring. Sexual reproduction involves two parents. Animals can be viviparous (they give birth to live young) or oviparous (they lay eggs). Asexual reproduction involves only one parent and is more common in plants.
Memory trick: ovi sounds like oval, the shape of an egg, so oviparous animals lay eggs. Vivi sounds like vivid and alive, so viviparous animals give birth to live young.

steps.caption: All living things are made up of cells. Cells are the basic units of life. They are so tiny that we can only see them through a microscope.

Living things can be multicellular or unicellular. Plants and animals are multicellular: they are made up of more than one cell. Bacteria are unicellular: they are made up of just one cell. Cells have different shapes and sizes: the cells of bacteria are the smallest, around 0.001 mm, while the alga called Acetabularia is a single cell of about 1 cm.
Memory trick: uni means one, like a unicorn with one horn, so unicellular means just one cell. Multi means many, so multicellular means more than one cell.
Cells have four parts in common: the nucleus, the cytoplasm, the organelles and the cell membrane. This is an animal cell.

steps.caption: Every sound is a vibration. Sound waves travel through the air from the thing that vibrates to your ears.

steps.caption: The central nervous system (CNS) is made of the brain and the spinal cord. The skull protects the brain, and the spine, or vertebral column, protects the spinal cord.

parts.label: brain
parts.info: The control centre of the body and part of the central nervous system (CNS).

parts.label: skull
parts.info: A hard case of bone that protects the brain.

parts.label: spinal cord
parts.info: A thick bundle of nerve fibres inside the spine, the other part of the CNS.

parts.label: spine
parts.info: The vertebral column, a chain of small bones that protects the spinal cord.

steps.caption: The peripheral nervous system (PNS) is all the nerves that connect the central nervous system with the rest of the body.

parts.label: nerves
parts.info: They form the peripheral nervous system (PNS), linking the CNS with every part of the body.

steps.caption: Nerves are made of neurons, or nerve cells. Each neuron has a cell body with a nucleus inside, the control centre of the cell.

parts.label: cell body
parts.info: The main part of the neuron, which keeps the cell alive.

parts.label: nucleus
parts.info: The control centre of the cell, inside the cell body.

steps.caption: Dendrites are short branches that receive messages. The axon is a long fibre that carries the message away from the cell body to the axon terminals.

parts.label: dendrites
parts.info: Short branches that receive messages, like doors in.

parts.label: axon
parts.info: A long fibre that carries the message away from the cell body.

parts.label: axon terminals
parts.info: The ends of the axon, which pass the message on to the next neuron.

steps.caption: Memory trick: the Axon sends the message Away; the Dendrites are the Doors where it comes in, and they branch like a tree.
A synapse is a tiny gap where a message passes from one neuron to the next. A nerve is a bundle of neuron fibres, like a cable full of wires.

parts.label: synapse
parts.info: A tiny gap where the message jumps from one neuron to the next.

steps.caption: Follow a message inside a neuron: it comes in through the dendrites, passes the cell body, runs along the axon to the axon terminals and jumps across the synapse to the next neuron.

Memory trick: Sensory nerves bring what you Sense into the CNS; Motor nerves make you Move by carrying orders from the CNS to the muscles. Receptors in the sense organs are where it all starts: they detect the stimuli.
A reflex act is very fast. If you touch something hot, the spinal cord orders the muscle to pull your hand away before the brain even notices.
